newsitem.title: JAPAN: LME transparency reforms possible this year -- Bagri.
newsitem.headline: LME transparency reforms possible this year -- Bagri.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange could take action to increase the market's transparency as early as the end of this year, LME chairman Raj Bagri said on Tuesday.
Asked if the LME might take action when Britain's Securities and Investments Board issues a report on the LME in late December, Bagri said, "It is possible at that time."

"We would like to make sure that we make those changes as quickly as we possibly can," Bagri said, although he also stressed the need to move carefully. "Some of these changes should be very carefully thought about.
"We are now in an ongoing dialogue with the industry...to see what more we can do. Our ideas in this respect will probably be more crystallised over the coming weeks," he said.

Asked about specific areas in which the LME may disclose more data, Bagri said, "Certainly the ownership of stocks, the total level of market positions, whether those positions are far forward or nearby, these are areas of concern to people and we have got to agree with the industry as to what kind of information we can make available."

He also reiterated the exchange's commitment to increasing transparency, which gained increased attention after the announcement in June that Sumitomo Corp had incurred massive losses from alleged unauthorised copper trading, much of which occurred on the LME.
"We at the exchange would like to provide more transparency," he said. "The difficulty is to define what you mean by transparency."
